testDesignCorrections: Initial B11/B12 fixtures used [v1, v3] with v2 omitted, intending to force a genuinely unresolvable target - but v1 is itself a valid (if inferential) chronological-predecessor candidate given v3's superseding-qualifier recital, so it legitimately resolved to v1 at REVIEW_REQUIRED/0.7 rather than staying UNRESOLVED. This is CORRECT production behavior (the deterministic layer correctly used the best available evidence, downgraded to REVIEW_REQUIRED because it is inferential), not a defect - fixed by using [v3] alone (no candidate document of the referenced type present at all) to exercise the genuinely-no-candidate DETERMINISTIC_NO_CANDIDATE path instead.

computeOperativeDocument's original notResolved filter required every restatement effect to have status === RESOLVED, which incorrectly blocked document-graph resolution whenever the underlying effect was REVIEW_REQUIRED (e.g. Unit B2's own deliberately-inferential chronological-predecessor resolution) even though it carried a real, unambiguous targetDocumentId. Fixed to require only a non-null targetDocumentId (the true 'genuinely unknown link' condition) - see chain.ts's own updated comment for the safety rationale distinguishing effect-level confidence from document-graph-level ambiguity.

fullPackageGraphAndAmendmentSuiteRegress.note: tests/contract-model/amendment-and-versioning.test.ts (a real-Postgres test querying prisma.amendmentEffect.findMany with no explicit orderBy) intermittently fails on row ORDER (not content) when run as part of a large combined suite - reproduced once during this session's broader regression run, passed on immediate re-run in isolation and in this 3-file combination. Classified FLAKY / PRE_EXISTING, same category as the baseline's own documented repro-connection-race.test.ts flake - the test lacks a deterministic orderBy and Postgres row order without one is not guaranteed; not caused by, and not in scope for, this remediation's production code changes (none of which write to the amendmentEffect table's persistence path).
